question: What is the main purpose of an incident report in a healthcare facility?

options.A: To calculate monthly staff performance evaluations
options.B: To provide a permanent record for the patient's bedside chart
options.C: To serve as evidence for criminal prosecution of staff
options.D: To document unexpected events for quality improvement

explanation: Incident reports are administrative tools designed to track unexpected events so the hospital can improve safety systems, not to punish workers or go into clinical notes. [learn more](BMP115_U4_T7#BMP115_U4_T7_h1)

question: Why should a midwife view an incident report as a tool for safety rather than punishment?

options.A: It completely replaces the need for verbal handovers
options.B: It guarantees immunity from all civil lawsuits
options.C: It helps management fix underlying system failures
options.D: It allows nurses to alter patient vital signs safely

explanation: By recording what went wrong honestly, the facility can look at equipment or staffing issues and fix them to protect future mothers and babies. [learn more](BMP115_U4_T7#BMP115_U4_T7_h1)

question: Which of these situations requires filling out a formal incident report?

options.A: A near miss where a medication error was caught before administration
options.B: A patient complaining that the ward food is too cold
options.C: A visitor arriving ten minutes after visiting hours end
options.D: Routine documentation of a normal spontaneous vaginal delivery

explanation: Near misses are critical events that must be reported because they highlight system vulnerabilities before a patient gets hurt. [learn more](BMP115_U4_T7#BMP115_U4_T7_h2)

question: A midwife notices the delivery room suction machine fails just as a newborn needs airway clearance. A backup machine is used right away and the baby is fine. What should the midwife do next?

options.A: Document the equipment failure only in the personal clinic diary
options.B: Ignore the event since the baby suffered no actual harm
options.C: Wait until the end of the month to mention it during a general meeting
options.D: File an incident report regarding the equipment failure

explanation: Even though the baby was unharmed, equipment failure during a critical procedure is a mandatory reporting event to ensure maintenance checks. [learn more](BMP115_U4_T7#BMP115_U4_T7_h2)

question: What essential detail must always be included at the top of an incident report?

options.A: The exact date, time, and specific hospital location
options.B: The personal home address of the attending doctor
options.C: The political affiliation of the patient's family
options.D: The financial status and insurance details of the patient

explanation: An accurate timeline and precise location are core elements needed to reconstruct the event and investigate properly. [learn more](BMP115_U4_T7#BMP115_U4_T7_h3)

question: Why is it important to record the exact job titles of all staff involved in an incident?

options.A: To clarify who was present and their specific responsibilities
options.B: To calculate hazard allowances for the monthly payroll
options.C: To ensure junior staff receive all the blame for system errors
options.D: To determine which staff members should be suspended immediately

explanation: Knowing who was there helps investigators understand clinical decision-making paths and identify areas needing more training support. [learn more](BMP115_U4_T7#BMP115_U4_T7_h3)

question: What is the very first step a midwife must take when an unexpected clinical incident happens?

options.A: Ensure immediate safety and care for the patient
options.B: Leave the ward immediately to write the report
options.C: Inform local journalists about the occurrence
options.D: Locate the hospital legal advisor for instructions

explanation: Patient safety and clinical stabilization always take absolute priority over filling out administrative paperwork. [learn more](BMP115_U4_T7#BMP115_U4_T7_h4)

question: Why should a midwife write an incident report as soon as possible after things settle down?

options.A: To ensure details remain fresh and accurate in memory
options.B: To fulfill a requirement before taking a lunch break
options.C: To prevent the patient from leaving the hospital early
options.D: To ensure the nursing supervisor leaves the shift on time

explanation: Writing down facts quickly prevents memory gaps and ensures the timeline remains precise. [learn more](BMP115_U4_T7#BMP115_U4_T7_h4)

question: Which of these phrases uses objective language suitable for an incident report?

options.A: The fetal heart rate dropped from 140 to 80 beats per minute at 14:15
options.B: The senior doctor acted carelessly and ignored the screaming patient
options.C: The lazy nurse forgot to check the intravenous line infusion
options.D: The patient was completely uncooperative and difficult to manage

explanation: Objective language states measurable facts and exact observations without adding emotional labels or insults. [learn more](BMP115_U4_T7#BMP115_U4_T7_h5)

question: Why is it incorrect to write a note in the patient's clinical chart stating that an incident report was filed?

options.A: It stops the doctor from writing any more prescriptions
options.B: It is illegal for midwives to mention administrative duties in charts
options.C: It mixes administrative risk management records with clinical care notes
options.D: It automatically makes the hospital liable in all civil court cases

explanation: Clinical charts are for medical care details, while incident reports are separate administrative documents kept out of standard patient files. [learn more](BMP115_U4_T7#BMP115_U4_T7_h5)

question: What should a midwife do with a completed incident report after finishing it?

options.A: Paste a copy on the public notice board for staff education
options.B: Keep it inside a personal handbag as protection against management
options.C: Give a copy directly to the patient's family members
options.D: Submit it through the proper confidential administrative channel

explanation: Incident reports are confidential internal documents and must be submitted through official administrative channels without unauthorized sharing. [learn more](BMP115_U4_T7#BMP115_U4_T7_h6)

question: Why must midwives keep the contents of an incident report strictly confidential?

options.A: Hospital management bans staff from reading their own writing
options.B: The documents can potentially be subpoenaed in legal proceedings
options.C: Patients have a legal right to burn the reports after discharge
options.D: Sharing reports reduces the monthly supply of stationery

explanation: Because these reports can sometimes be requested by courts during lawsuits, keeping them secure and confidential is crucial for legal protection. [learn more](BMP115_U4_T7#BMP115_U4_T7_h6)
